summary: This lecture is part 41 of a detailed explanation of Ibn al-Qayyim's seminal work "Zadul-Ma'ad" (Provisions for the Hereafter), which comprehensively covers the Sunnah of Prophet Muhammad across five volumes. The speaker explains the methodology and structure of this monumental 3000+ page work that was written entirely from memory during Ibn al-Qayyim's journey to Hajj. The lecture transitions from discussing the Prophet's visitation of the sick to his handling of the dead, covering Islamic funeral practices including the ritual bathing (ghusl), shrouding, and funeral prayer (Salat al-Janazah). The speaker emphasizes the proper procedure for preparing a deceased Muslim's body while clarifying contemporary applications of Prophetic practices.
